PROPOSED: Every entity, surface-form list, kind tag and modellable flag below is PROPOSED BY THE SYSTEM and counts for nothing until a human verifies it against the chapter (D-048). This is the hand-label set the 3A gate measures precision and recall against.
how_to_verify: Read chapter.json. For each entity: is it genuinely named (not merely implied)? Are surface_forms and naming_chunks right and complete? Is anything named in the chapter missing? Check the excluded_candidates table: does the rule that excluded each one give the answer you would give? If you disagree with an inclusion or exclusion, the RULE changes, not the label — see label_rules. Then set verified: true with your name and date.

certification.note: Every 3A number measured against this set is certified against the model and chapter named here and nothing else (same treatment as D-058). A model change or a chapter change invalidates it.
certification.label_set_commit: DERIVED BY THE RUNNER at measurement time: git log -1 --format=%h -- this file. Hand-typing it is impossible (a commit cannot contain its own hash) and a stale value would certify against the wrong labels.

SCOPE_LIMITS.read_this_before_quoting_any_number: Same two limits as the provenance golden set, and they bound every 3A number the same way.
SCOPE_LIMITS.1_this_is_a_ceiling_not_a_typical_case: One OpenStax section: clean, digital-native, professionally edited, English, with consistent terminology and no OCR noise. Aakar's real input is scanned Indian textbooks. Extraction precision and recall measured here are close to the best this system will do on any chapter; they say nothing about the rate on the actual corpus. What they establish is that failures seen on a clean chapter are real, since the input cannot be blamed for them.
SCOPE_LIMITS.2_no_ocr_noise_in_the_names: Every surface form here is spelled the way the model expects. A scanned page produces 'ciliary hody', 'vitre0us humor', split words across a line break — and an extractor that verifies claims by whole-word match against chunk text will DROP a correct entity whose only naming chunk is garbled. That is a recall failure invisible on this chapter. Future work, same as the provenance set: one chapter of real Tesseract output over a real scanned page.

provenance_of_these_labels: Candidates were listed by reading the chapter — every noun phrase a reader might call a structure, INCLUDING the ones taste would reject, so the exclusion rule gets exercised (R2). surface_forms, naming_chunks and occurrence counts were then derived MECHANICALLY by the same whole-word matcher provenance resolution uses (aakar/rag/provenance_resolve.py), and the label rules below were applied mechanically. The judgment calls that remain are the candidate list itself, each entity's kind, and modellable.

label_rules.why_mechanical: Architect ruling: a boundary decided by taste is not reproducible. A future chapter must be labelled the same way by a different person, or by a script. If a verifier disagrees with an outcome below, the rule is amended and re-applied to every candidate; the label is never hand-flipped.
label_rules.R0_scope: A candidate must be a physical constituent of the organism — something that can be assigned a `kind` from kind_vocabulary. Processes (photoreception), properties (visual acuity, membrane potential), quantities, and external stimuli (light, light energy) have no kind and are out of scope. This is the one rule that requires a human to assign a kind; the assignment is recorded per entity so it is auditable.
label_rules.R1_generic_mention: A candidate is EXCLUDED as a generic mention if ALL THREE hold: (a) every surface form the chapter uses for it has a head noun in CATEGORY_NOUNS; (b) its total occurrences across all surface forms, whole-word, is at most 1; (c) no occurrence is introduced by a NAMING_CONSTRUCTION. Otherwise it is included. Evaluated over SURFACE FORMS, not the canonical name: the chapter names retinal ganglion cells only as 'RGCs', whose head is not a category noun, so it is included — whereas testing the canonical name would exclude it on the head 'cell'. The rule is about how the chapter names the thing.
NAMING_CONSTRUCTIONS: or (the|a|an)? X,  (appositive: 'the neural tunic, or retina,')
label_rules.R1_ASYMMETRY_recorded_not_fixed: Architect ruling 2026-09-02. Exclusion requires a category-noun head, so a candidate with a NON-category head is included at ANY occurrence count: 'infolding' and 'axon' are included at one mention while 'cell membrane' is excluded at one mention. This is a known property of the rule, kept deliberately. Adding an occurrence threshold for non-category heads would be taste wearing a rule's clothes. The three weak inclusions (photosensitive pigment, axon, infolding) stand; a future verifier should read this as designed, not as an oversight.
label_rules.R2_one_entity_many_forms: Two names for one structure are ONE entity with several surface forms (architect ruling 3: retina / neural tunic). The curation gate counts structures; counting one twice inflates the denominator.
label_rules.R4_locative: Architect ruling 2026-09-02, after the first live run extracted 'Anterior segment of eye' from 'the anterior eye' (c04). A candidate is EXCLUDED as a location if any of its in-chapter surface forms is a purely POSITIONAL modifier applied to a string that is ITSELF a listed entity. Keyed on the modifier, not the head: anterior + eye -> 'eye' is an entity -> EXCLUDE; outer + segment -> 'segment' is not -> KEEP. Without that second clause R4 eats 'outer segment', which is real. Evaluated over surface forms like R1, because the model's canonical name was not positional + entity while its chapter form was.
label_rules.R4_KNOWN_LIMITATION_recorded_not_fixed: A genuinely named structure of the same shape - 'inner ear' where 'ear' is an entity, 'lateral ventricle', 'distal tubule' - would be excluded by R4. No such case exists in this chapter. A future verifier who meets one should read it as designed; amending R4 (an occurrence or naming-construction prong, as in R1) is the architect's ruling to make.
label_rules.R4_REAPPLIED: Re-applied mechanically to every entity in this set and every candidate the extractor proposed: exactly one candidate moved (the extractor's 'Anterior segment of eye'); none of the 28 verified entities moved, including 'outer segment', 'anterior cavity' and 'posterior cavity', whose remainders are not entities. Reported because a rule that only ever fires once is indistinguishable from a hand-flip - the runner re-checks and prints this on every run.
label_rules.R3_no_shared_surface_form: No surface form may be claimed by two entities, by any route — rule-generated inflection, model synonym, or one of each. A collision is a DEFECT, not a warning: it fails extraction rather than picking a winner, because silent resolution surfaces later as provenance behaviour nobody can explain (architect ruling). This label set is checked against R3 before it is used.

modellable.definition: Whether a spec at THIS TOPIC'S SCALE — the whole eye, as in specs/golden/human_eye — could reasonably include the entity as a distinct clickable geometry. Topic-relative by construction: a 'photoreceptor' topic would model rods and cones; a whole-eye topic would not.
modellable.why_it_exists: Coverage has two distinct failure modes. The chapter names it and the spec omitted it: a defect the curator must act on. The chapter names it and it is outside the model's scope: correct, and not the curator's problem. Collapsing them makes the coverage panel unreadable. 3B's coverage metric reports them separately, and its denominator for 'omitted' is the modellable: true entities only.

method_caveats.singular_recovery_is_fit_to_this_chapter: Architect ruling 2026-09-02: singular recovery (a plural the model copied from the text also emits its singular when the chapter contains it whole-word) is SWITCHED ON. It took alias coverage from 24/27 to 27/27 - measured on the chapter the rule was designed against. That is fitting to the test set, so 27/27 is optimistic and is printed as such on every run. A second chapter is what would make it a measurement.
method_caveats.synonym_guard_is_name_choice_sensitive_O: The precision guard's outcome depends on which canonical names the model picks: 'photoreceptor' falls to the own-name rule when the entity is named 'Photoreceptor cell' and to the head-noun rule when rods are named 'Rod photoreceptor'. The refined guard was a null result on this chapter. Kept OPEN by ruling - a real property of the method that a second chapter may make non-null.

gate_reporting.ruling: Architect 2026-09-02. Precision and recall are each reported TWICE: over all named entities, and over modellable: true only. The second is the product-relevant number and the one 3B's coverage denominator matches; the first tells you what the extractor misses. Both as counts, never a score.
gate_reporting.modellable_proposed_is_not_fed_to_3B: Architect ruling 2026-09-02. The model's modellable guess agreed with the verified labels 25/27, but both disagreements were the humours - the exact class where the judgement was hardest and ruling 1 had to decide. A signal systematically wrong on the difficult class is worse than no signal in a coverage denominator. It is emitted as `modellable_proposed`, recorded, and not read by 3B; a second chapter may measure it later.
gate_reporting.matching: An extracted entity matches a labelled one when their normalised surface-form sets intersect (name + aliases on the extracted side, name + surface_forms here), after the deterministic inflector is applied to both sides so that humor/humour and RGC/RGCs link. Unmatched entities on either side are listed by name, so a near-miss is visible rather than counted silently.

entities.note: R2: 'neural tunic' is the chapter's own second name for the retina (c05), so one entity.

entities.name: ciliary body
entities.note: Head 'body' is a category noun; included by R1(b) — three occurrences.

entities.name: aqueous humor
entities.note: Ruling 1: substances in. Introduced by a naming construction ('called the aqueous humor').

entities.name: vitreous humor
entities.note: Ruling 1: a student will click the vitreous humour. Introduced by a naming construction.

entities.name: photoreceptor
entities.note: Ruling 4: named but not modelled at whole-eye scale.

entities.name: rod
entities.note: 'rod-shaped' matches whole-word on 'rod' because the hyphen is a word boundary. That is correct here — the sentence is about rods — and it is exactly the kind of matcher behaviour R3's collision check has to reason about.

entities.name: membrane-bound disc
entities.note: No bare 'disc' claimed, so no collision with optic disc.

entities.name: photosensitive pigment
entities.note: INCLUDED BY RULE, not by taste. Head 'pigment' is a category noun, but it occurs twice, so R1(b) fails and it stays. Rhodopsin is its named instance; distinct surface forms, so no R3 collision. RULED 2026-09-02: stands (see R1_ASYMMETRY).

entities.name: retinal ganglion cell
entities.note: THE HARD CASE. The full name appears nowhere; the chapter writes only 'RGCs'. Included by R1 evaluated over surface forms (head 'RGCs' is not a category noun). An extractor emitting the full name without the abbreviation alias scores zero provenance on the only chunk naming it.

entities.name: axon
entities.note: INCLUDED BY RULE. 'The axons of RGCs' are the subject of c10's sentence and the head is not a category noun. At whole-eye scale the optic nerve is modelled and its axons are not. RULED 2026-09-02: stands (see R1_ASYMMETRY).

entities.name: infolding
entities.note: INCLUDED BY RULE — 'infoldings of the cell membrane' in cone outer segments. The weakest inclusion on the list, kept precisely because the rule says so and the rule, not the label, is what a verifier corrects. RULED 2026-09-02: stands (see R1_ASYMMETRY).

excluded_candidates.head: muscle
excluded_candidates.note: 'The iris is a smooth muscle' is a classification, not a naming construction.

Proposed by the extractor on the first live run, not by the human candidate list. 'anterior eye' is positional + 'eye', a listed entity: a location, not a structure. Added here by rule, never by hand - hand-adding 'anterior segment' to the entities would have been the label-flipping label_rules forbids.
